generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from parent key pool; NULL only when the column is nullable and not part of a primary key; ensure some parent rows have no children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Uniform integer in [1, 10000]; include boundary values from per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_distance: Uniform integer in [100, 9000]; include boundary values from per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_price: Uniform decimal in [50.00, 2000.00] rounded to 2 decimals; include boundary values from per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.decimal_salary: Uniform decimal in [30000.00, 300000.00] rounded to 2 decimals; include boundary values from per_column_exceptions.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random combination of first/last name tokens; 5% near-duplicate variants (case/whitespace) of existing values; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_city: Random pick from a fixed city pool; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_aircraft_name: Random pick from a fixed aircraft model pool; 5% near-duplicate variants; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.date_datetime: Random datetime in 2005-01-01..2005-12-31; format 'MM/DD/YYYY HH24:MI'; 5% NULL when nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_share: For DISTINCT-target columns, ensure duplicate share 20-50% by repeating values from a small pool.
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: For GROUP-target columns, ensure groups of size 1, 2, and >=3 exist; for numeric columns repeat existing numeric values, for string columns repeat existing string values; never inject non-typed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.order_ties: For ORDER-target columns, plant ties at the listed rank (e.g., two rows with equal COUNT).
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: Each nullable column gets at least one NULL row; share follows compact DB null_rate (0% observed, so plant 1 NULL row per nullable column).
generic_sampling_rules.rows_with_different_values: For MAX/MIN scalar-target columns, ensure at least two rows per group carry different values so the aggregate is non-trivial.

supporting_evidence.flight.arrival_date >= flight.departure_: All 8 shown flight rows satisfy arrival_date >= departure_date (e.g., flno 2: 09:40 >= 09:30; flno 7: 08:45 >= 08:45).
supporting_evidence.flight.distance > 0: All shown flight distances are positive (2308, 1749, 1251, 2606, 7487, 5478, 2551, 802).
supporting_evidence.aircraft.distance > 0: All shown aircraft distances are positive (8430, 3383, 7120, 1502, 1530, 2128, 520, 4103).

uncertainty: No formula relating flight.distance to aircraft.distance or price to distance was verified on all shown rows; no offset/rate formula is stated. Nullable columns show 0% null_rate in the compact DB, but at least one NULL row per nullable column is planted per instruction 10. certificate.aid is part of the primary key (eid, aid) and is therefore NOT NULL; the certificate.aid null_rows pattern is dropped. flight.aid is nullable in the DDL and is the only null_target. Primary-key columns aircraft.aid and employee.eid cannot carry duplicates or group sizes > 1; those patterns are dropped for them and reinterpreted on the referencing FK columns (flight.aid, certificate.aid, certificate.eid).
